summary: The root LWY primarily signifies bending, twisting, or turning something. It can also denote evading, delaying, or distorting.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.

headwords.gloss: He waited for him; He went along, not pausing nor waiting for any one; i. q

parts.t: He went along, not pausing nor waiting for any one.
affair, difficult and intricate to him:
He concealed his affair from me.

headwords.def: لَوَى عَلَيْهِ He waited for him. (Msb.) مَرَّ لَا يَلْوِى عَلَى أَحَدٍ He went along, not pausing nor waiting for any one. (Msb.) See the Kur-án, iii. 147. لَوَاهُ بِدَيْنِهِ i. q. مَطَلَهُ . (S, Msb, K.) لَوَى He twisted a thing; turned or wreathed it round or about: contorted it: wound it: curled it: curved it: or bent it. (K, &c.) And He, or it, turned him from his course; made him to deviate, or swerve. لَوَى عَلَيْهِ He went round it, or round about it. (Bd, in liii. 20.) لَوَى عَلَيْهِ أَمْرَهُ [ He mode his case, or affair, difficult and intricate to him: see إِلْتَوّى عَلَيْهِ ]. (S, K, art. عوص .) لَوَى خَبَرَهُ , (assumed tropical:) He concealed his information. (T, TA.) And لَوَى أَمْرَهُ عِنِّى (tropical:) He concealed his affair from me.

headwords.gloss: He distorted, wrested; wrung, the language

parts.t: , if the verb be correctly thus: see

headwords.def: أَلْوَى بِالكَلَامِ He distorted, wrested, or wrung, the language. (M, K.) [Hence, perhaps, فُلَانٌ يُلْوِى بِخَصْمِهِ , if the verb be correctly thus: see عُقْمِىَ , last sentence.]

headwords.gloss: It twisted; coiled, itself; it became twisted

parts.t: He writhed by reason of the pain of beating

headwords.def: تَلَوَّى ألوى لوى لوي تلو تلوى تلوي It twisted, or coiled, itself: (KL:) it became twisted, or coiled: one says, تَلَوَّتِ الحَيَّةُ . (MA.) تَلَوَّى مِنْ وَجَعِ الضَّرْبِ [ He writhed by reason of the pain of beating ]. (M, A, K, art. ضور .)
يَتَلاَوَيَانِ said of two serpents [ They twist together ]: see عَقاَمٌ , last sentence.

headwords.gloss: It twisted: wound: bent; became difficult; difficult and intricate

parts.t: My want became difficult of attainment.

headwords.def: اِلْتَوَى , neuter verb, It twisted: wound: bent. (K, &c.) اِلْتَوَى عَلَيْهِ It (an affair) became difficult; or difficult and intricate. (TA.) الْتَوَتْ عَلَىَّ حَاجَتِى My want became difficult of attainment. (TA.) التوى عَلَيْهِ also He acted, or behaved, perversely towards him.

headwords.gloss: A banner; standard; of a commander

parts.t: of an army, less than the
being a strip of cloth, twisted,
wound, and tied to a spear-shaft.

headwords.def: لِوَآءٌ A banner, or standard, syn. عَلَمٌ , (M, Mgh, K,) of a commander, (T,) or of an army, less than the رَايَة , being a strip of cloth, twisted, or wound, and tied to a spear-shaft. (Mgh.) See رِفَادَةٌ . Respecting the لِوَآء of the Kaabeh, see سَدَنَ and فَادَةٌ .
اللَّوَا occurs in poetry for اللَّوَاتِى . (TA in art. شرف .)
أَلْوَى Very contentious. (K.) See an ex. voce مُسْتَمَرّ .

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
